newsitem.title: USA: Clinton campaigns as questions about funds arise.
newsitem.headline: Clinton campaigns as questions about funds arise.

text.p: Buoyed by polls suggesting he may have the Nov. 5 election won, President Bill Clinton campaigned in Republican strongholds on Thursday as new questions arose about a senior Democratic fundraiser's ties to the White House.

In Arizona, which no Democratic presidential candidate has won since 1948, Clinton stuck to "family values" issues that have helped him among two groups that could turn the tide here next Tuesday -- elderly voters and young people focused on crime, health, education and the economy.
Speaking at a sun-drenched rally on the futuristic campus of Arizona State University, Clinton said the United States was "moving in the right direction."

"Compared to four years ago we have 10 and a half million more jobs, we have the lowest combined rates of unemployment, inflation and home mortgage interest in 27 years," he said. "The deficit has been cut in all four years of my administration for the first time in the 20th century."

Clinton said he was against "what my opponent has advocated -- cutting student loans and abolishing the Department of Education." And assailing Dole's opposition to his anti-crime programme, he boasted that "the crime rate is down for four years in a row and is now at a 10-year low."
Former New York City police commissioner William Bratton shared the platform with the president and reinforced Clinton's anti-crime message by endorsing the 50-year-old Democrat.
"On Tuesday he'll get my vote for four more years because of the leadership he's given us over the last four," Bratton said.

Clinton later flew on to conservative Nevada, another state normally hostile to Democratic presidential candidates, before ending the day in California, the biggest prize in his contest with Republican Bob Dole.

Asked if the president's effort to carry marginal states meant that Clinton was confident he had the 270 electoral votes needed to win next Tuesday all locked up, deputy campaign director Fred DuVal said: "We're not neglecting our base; we've simply expanded it to a larger universe."

A new poll showed Clinton widening his lead in California despite a make-or-break effort by Dole to pull off a stunning upset by carrying the country's most populous state with its 54 electoral votes.

The poll by the independent Field Institute showed Clinton leading Dole 52 percent to 34 percent in California. Dole decided to stake his hopes of victory on an all-out push in the state after earlier polls appeared to show him narrowing the gap on Clinton there.

All national polls are giving Clinton a lead of between 10 and 18 points, except for the Reuters/Zogby tracking poll, which has Dole closing the gap to 7.7 points in recent days. Clinton campaign aides said their own internal polling did not indicate such an erosion of the present's support.

Clinton's apparent march to victory was clouded by swirling new questions about controversial Democratic fundraiser John Huang, who was suspended from his job amid reports that he unlawfully solicited foreign contributions.
The Washington Post and New York Times reported on Thursday that Huang made at least 78 visits to the White House since July 1, 1995.
Citing records kept by the Secret Service, the Post said the number of visits suggested Huang had a closer connection to the White House than was previously known.

But White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Huang's visits could have included "seeing a friend, going to a meeting (or) attending a large reception," and insisted they were "consistent with his responsibilities" as a Commerce Department official and later as a party fundraiser.

A senior administration official accompanying Clinton said the reports were "making a mountain out of a molehill" and that Huang was "involved in fundraising and did outreach to the Asian-American community, which is of growing importance" as a voting block.
Clinton was to tackle the issue of campaign finance reform in a major speech in Santa Barbara, California on Friday.
